questions.prompt: Where was the ladder taken when the new scoreboard was installed?

stimulus.title: The Two Scoreboards
stimulus.body:
At a cricket ground near Bendigo, the wooden scoreboard had stood for decades. Its painted numbers had faded to the colour of weak tea. Every Saturday, the scorer, Mr Vale, climbed a narrow ladder to slide new cards into place. When the council installed a digital board, the ladder was carried into the equipment shed.

I expected everyone to celebrate. The new figures blazed like tiny white windows, clear even from the far boundary. Yet on its first morning, Mr Vale lingered beside the empty wooden frame, rolling a scorecard between his fingers. He had spent years listening for the umpire's call before changing each number.

During the second over, the screen faltered: its figures went dark for a moment, then returned. "Just a hiccup," said the groundskeeper, although she kept glancing towards it. Later, a shower sent spectators under the shelter. Nobody needed to climb the slippery ladder, and the score remained visible through the rain.

After the match, Mr Vale showed a younger volunteer how to check the screen against the paper scorebook. "Bright numbers can still be wrong," he said. He smiled at the new board, but slipped his old scorecard into his pocket.

options.text: To the far boundary
Under the shelter
Beside the wooden frame
Into the equipment shed

questions.explanation: The opening paragraph explicitly states that the ladder was carried into the equipment shed. The reader must distinguish this location from other places mentioned in the passage.
